headline: Europe's top central banker is leaving eight months early.
summary: The European Central Bank said Wednesday that its president, Christine Lagarde, will step down in February, eight months before her term ends. The rumour had run since January. Reuters reports she may go on to lead the World Economic Forum. EU officials want her successor picked before France votes for a president in April.
cover_answer: Reuters says a new job: running the World Economic Forum.
table_question: Is quitting early fine if you give eight months' notice?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Christine Lagarde, who runs the bank that looks after Europe's money, said on Wednesday she will leave her job in February, sooner than planned. Her bank keeps prices steady, the way a thermostat keeps a room from getting too hot. Nothing changes for your money today. The grown-ups there are picking who comes next.
5-7.why: A thermostat, nothing changing at home, someone picking who is next.
5-7.why_long: A child this age reasons from what is in front of them, so the script turns a central bank into a thermostat, a dial they know. What they want to know is whether this reaches them, so nothing changes for your money comes before the name. Expect "did she get fired?" No. She resigned, with eight months' notice.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Christine Lagarde runs the European Central Bank, which sets the cost of borrowing across Europe, like a thermostat for prices. On Wednesday it said she leaves in February, eight months early. Prices are rising, Semafor says, so leaders want her successor chosen before France votes in April.
8-12.why: Thermostat, rising prices, an election. One chain.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out chains of cause and effect, so the script hands them one: prices are rising, the bank that steadies them is losing its head, so leaders want the next one chosen before a vote. The thermostat is the mechanism they know. Expect "why does an election matter?" The far right is expected to win it.

13-17.script: If you ran Europe's central bank, would you leave eight months early for a bigger job? Reuters says Lagarde may go on to lead the World Economic Forum. Second: EU officials want her successor picked before France's April election, which the far right is expected to win. Prudent, or a way around voters?
13-17.why: A bigger job, and a vote worked around. Two things to hold.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a leader may leave early for a better job, and the people replacing her may be hurrying to beat an election. The script asks whether that hurry is prudence or a dodge, and the argument improves once they take a side. Expect "who picks the next one?" EU leaders, before April.

5-7.a: No. Nothing about your money changes. She leaves her job in February and someone else takes it.

8-12.q: What does a central bank do?
8-12.a: It sets the cost of borrowing, which helps keep prices steady.

8-12.q: Why does the French election matter?
8-12.a: Leaders want her successor picked before France votes in April.

13-17.a: Reuters says a new job, running the World Economic Forum.

13-17.q: Is it fair to pick her successor before France votes?
13-17.a: That is the argument. Officials want it done before April's vote.
